extracted.intended_audience: food/feed manufacturers, animal food ingredient formulators, regulatory affairs professionals, and legal/regulatory stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Final rule amending 21 CFR part 573 to update the organism name from Pichia pastoris to Komagataella pastoris and to clarify that the dried yeast is non-viable and subject to a maximum usage level in broiler chicken feed formulations. The document provides the regulatory text amendments, effective date, authority citation, and the agency's procedural finding regarding notice-and-comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity of the food additive (organism name)
rubrics_metrics.description: The food additive Komagataella pastoris dried yeast is non-viable and may be used in feed formulations of broiler chickens as a source of protein not to exceed 10 percent by weight of the total formulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision updates the organism name from Pichia pastoris to Komagataella pastoris to improve accuracy of the regulations. The identity statement appears in the revised regulatory text (§ 573.587(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-viability requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The food additive Komagataella pastoris dried yeast is non-viable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation explicitly clarifies that the yeast is non-viable in the market formulation. This is a specification of the allowable physical/biological state of the additive in commerce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum usage level in feed formulations
rubrics_metrics.description: May be used in feed formulations of broiler chickens as a source of protein not to exceed 10 percent by weight of the total formulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets a quantitative upper limit on inclusion rate (10% by weight) for broiler chicken feed formulations; formulators must ensure compliance with this percentage limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory text amendment and section redesignation
rubrics_metrics.description: Redesignate § 573.750 as § 573.587 and amend newly redesignated § 573.587 by revising the section heading and paragraph (a) to read as follows: § 573.587 Komagataella pastoris dried yeast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions for how the Code of Federal Regulations will be changed: renumbering (redesignation) and replacement of the section heading and paragraph text. Administrative/technical amendment rather than substantive policy change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when the amended regulatory requirements (section redesignation and revised identity/limits) become legally effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency determination on notice-and-comment (APA) applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication of this document constitutes final action under the Administrative Procedure Act (5 U.S.C. 553). FDA has determined that notice and public comment are unnecessary because this amendment to the regulations provides only technical changes including updating scientific nomenclature and is nonsubstantive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal/procedural rationale: the agency treats the amendment as a technical, nonsubstantive change and therefore declines to undertake notice-and-comment rulemaking. This explains the procedural posture and legal basis for immediate final action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority citation
rubrics_metrics.description: The authority citation for part 573 continues to read as follows: Authority: 21 U.S.C. 321, 342, 348.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the statutory grants of authority under which the FDA issues and amends the food additive regulations; relevant for legal/administrative context and for those assessing agency power to make the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document identification and docket information
rubrics_metrics.description: Docket No. FDA-2024-F-3882; Document Number 2024-19856; Document Citation 89 FR 72315.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the official Federal Register citation and docket identifiers to locate the full rulemaking record, correspondence, and any related documents. Useful for regulatory compliance, tracking, and recordkeeping.
